WITH order_types AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT o.recordvault, o.ordertune
  FROM orderexecutions oe
  INNER JOIN orders o ON oe.ordersmark = o.recordvault
),
order_counts AS (
  SELECT ordertune, COUNT(*) as order_count
  FROM order_types
  GROUP BY ordertune
),
total_count AS (
  SELECT SUM(order_count) as total FROM order_counts
),
order_shares AS (
  SELECT
    oc.ordertune,
    oc.order_count,
    CAST(oc.order_count AS FLOAT) / tc.total as share
  FROM order_counts oc
  CROSS JOIN total_count tc
),
avg_share_calc AS (
  SELECT AVG(share) as avg_share FROM order_shares
),
filtered_types AS (
  SELECT os.order_count, os.share
  FROM order_shares os
  CROSS JOIN avg_share_calc asc
  WHERE os.share > asc.avg_share
)
SELECT
  SUM(order_count) as sum_of_counts,
  AVG(share) as avg_share,
  AVG(share) - (SELECT avg_share FROM avg_share_calc) as avg_excess
FROM filtered_types;

assumptions.assumption: DISTINCT on (recordvault, ordertune) eliminates duplicate order-type pairs when an order has multiple executions, ensuring each order is counted once per type.
NULL values for ordertune are included as a separate group per standard SQL GROUP BY behavior.

Average share is the arithmetic mean of shares across all distinct order types; the average excess is then the mean of (share − overall_average_share) for filtered types, which equals avg_share_of_filtered − overall_average.
